# APAC H2H Connectivity: Architecture and Bank-Protocol Matrix

**Prepared:** 10 October 2026 · **Scope:** DBS, OCBC, UOB, HSBC, Standard Chartered, Citi, J.P. Morgan, MUFG, Mizuho, ANZ, CBA · **Method:** public sources only

Companion files: `APAC_Connectivity_Landscape_v2.md` (full capability and reference table), `APAC_H2H_Protocols_and_Architecture.md` (H2H-only table with Mermaid diagrams) and `APAC_H2H_Transport_Rails_Architecture.svg` (the diagram below as a standalone vector file).

---

## 1. Architecture: client to bank over H2H transport rails

A client ERP or TMS sends payment files to the bank over one of six transport rails. The bank's H2H gateway receives them, maps and validates them per client, optionally hands approval to online banking, then passes them to the payment engine. Acknowledgements, status and statements return on the same rail (dashed line).

![H2H architecture: client ERP/TMS to six transport rails (SFTP + PGP, AS2, FTPS and HTTPS, EBICS, SWIFT, not published), then bank-side H2H gateway, map and validate, optional approval, payment engine, and acknowledgements returning to the client][arch-png]

### Text version (renders in any viewer)

```text
     Client side                   Transport rails                      Bank side

                            ┌───────────────────────────┐       ┌──────────────────────┐
                        ┌──►│ SFTP over SSH + PGP       │───┬──►│ H2H gateway          │
                        │   ├───────────────────────────┤   │   │ folders · keys       │
┌───────────────────┐   ├──►│ AS2 over HTTP/S           │───┤   └──────────────────────┘
│                   │   │   ├───────────────────────────┤   │              │
│ Client ERP/TMS    │   ├──►│ FTPS and HTTPS (SOAP)     │───┤              ▼
│ SAP, Oracle, TMS  ├───┤   ├───────────────────────────┤   │   ┌──────────────────────┐
│                   │   ├──►│ EBICS                     │───┤   │ Map + validate       │
│                   │   │   ├───────────────────────────┤   │   │ per-client rules     │
└───────────────────┘   ├──►│ SWIFT FileAct / FIN       │───┤   └──────────────────────┘
          ▲             │   ├───────────────────────────┤   │              │
          │             └──►│ Protocol not published    │───┘              ▼
          │                 └───────────────────────────┘       ┌──────────────────────┐
          │                                                     │ Approval             │
          │                                                     │ optional hand-off    │
          │                                                     └──────────────────────┘
          │                                                                │
          │                                                                ▼
          │                                                     ┌──────────────────────┐
          │                                                     │ Payment engine       │
          │                                                     │ clearing, posting    │
          │                                                     └──────────────────────┘
          │                                                                │
          │                                                                ▼
          │                                                     ┌──────────────────────┐
          │                                                     │ Ack + status         │
          │                                                     │ statements back      │
          │                                                     └──────────┬───────────┘
          ┌─── acks, status and statements return on the same rail ────────┘
```

How to read the diagram:

- In the image, purple boxes are transport rails, teal boxes are bank-side processing and gray boxes are neutral or optional.
- "Protocol not published" covers banks that offer H2H but do not state the transport on the pages I found: OCBC, MUFG GPH (Internet), Mizuho and SC (H2H).
- The approval hand-off is optional and exists at UOB (BIBPlus), ANZ (Hybrid via Transactive Global) and SC (online release).

## 2. Bank-protocol matrix

Which banks publicly confirm each H2H transport rail:

| Bank | SFTP | PGP | AS2 | FTPS / HTTPS | EBICS | SWIFT |
|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| DBS | ✔\* | ✔\* | – | – | – | ✔ |
| OCBC | – | – | – | – | – | ✔ |
| UOB | ✔ | ✔ | – | – | – | ✔ |
| HSBC | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | – | – |
| Standard Chartered | – | – | – | – | ✔ | ✔ |
| Citi | ✔ | – | ✔ | ✔ | – | ✔ |
| J.P. Morgan | ✔ | ✔\* | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | – |
| MUFG | – | – | – | – | – | ✔ |
| Mizuho | – | – | – | – | – | ✔ |
| ANZ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔† | – | – | ✔ |
| CBA | ✔ | – | – | – | – | – |
| **Banks confirming** | **7 of 11** | **5 of 11** | **4 of 11** | **3 of 11** | **2 of 11** | **8 of 11** |

Legend: ✔ confirmed on a bank page · ✔\* confirmed only through a third-party source (DBS customer story; J.P. Morgan connectivity guide copy) · ✔† appears only in a glossary (ANZ lists AS2 but does not confirm it as offered) · – not confirmed in the pages I found, which does not mean the bank lacks it. J.P. Morgan and CBA SWIFT connectivity were not researched. HSBC SWIFT connectivity appears only in dated sources and is shown as a dash.

What the matrix shows (my reading):

- SWIFT is the most widely confirmed rail (8 of 11 banks), followed by SFTP (7 of 11).
- Six banks publish transport detail on their own pages: UOB, HSBC, Citi, J.P. Morgan, ANZ and CBA. DBS shows it only through a customer story. OCBC, Standard Chartered, MUFG and Mizuho publish none on the pages found.
- Counting only the rails marked above, J.P. Morgan lists five and HSBC, Citi and ANZ four each (ANZ's count includes the glossary-only AS2; J.P. Morgan SWIFT was not researched).
- PGP is confirmed at five banks (DBS, UOB, HSBC, J.P. Morgan, ANZ), and all five pair it with SFTP.

## 4. Notes and limitations

- Public sources only; bank pages can be region-specific. Citi protocol detail comes from an EMEA page.
- DBS protocol detail comes from a third-party customer story; the J.P. Morgan connectivity guide is a third-party copy of a bank document.
- Absence of a rail in the matrix reflects what the pages I read state, not what the bank supports.
- The image above is embedded in this file. If your viewer does not display it, use the text version or the standalone SVG file.
